cues.en: The Netherlands is a great place if you don't want to drive.
cues.zh: 如果你不想开车，荷兰是个极好的地方。

cues.en: There are lots of areas that are pedestrianized and nearly car-free.
cues.zh: 这里有大片步行街，几乎见不到汽车。

cues.en: Trains are so pervasive and frequent that they work almost like a country-wide metro system.
cues.zh: 火车网络极其密集且车次频繁，运作起来简直就像覆盖全国的地铁系统。

cues.en: Plus rail stations have giant bicycle parking garages and high-quality public transit connections to get you to your final destination.
cues.zh: 此外，火车站不仅有巨大的自行车停车场，还有高质量的公共交通接驳，能送你到达最终目的地。

cues.en: and there are bicycle paths almost everywhere. In many cases cyclists can
cues.zh: 而且自行车道几乎无处不在。很多时候，骑行者可以

cues.en: take the fastest and most direct route to where they're going while drivers
cues.zh: 走最快、最直接的路线到达目的地，而司机

cues.en: need to take the long way around. I get a lot of comments on this channel by
cues.zh: 却不得不绕远路。我经常在这个频道收到一些评论，

cues.en: people who say that they love cars and would hate to live somewhere like this,
cues.zh: 有人说他们喜欢汽车，绝对讨厌生活在这样的地方，

cues.en: but what they don't realize is that driving is awesome in the Netherlands.
cues.zh: 但他们没意识到的是，在荷兰开车其实棒极了。

cues.en: This summer I traveled to Canada to visit family and I did a lot of driving
cues.zh: 今年夏天我去加拿大探亲，

cues.en: while I was there.
cues.zh: 在那期间开了不少车。

cues.en: After almost two years away, it was a real shock to go from the comfortable civilized
cues.zh: 时隔将近两年，从荷兰舒适文明的

cues.en: driving experience in the Netherlands to driving in Canada.
cues.zh: 驾驶体验换到加拿大开车，着实让我震惊不小。

cues.en: It made me appreciate how good we have it here.
cues.zh: 这让我意识到我们这里的环境有多好。

cues.en: I'm not the only one who thinks this either.
cues.zh: 而且有这种想法的并不只有我一个。

cues.en: Take for example the YouTube channel Kerlim, an American and self-professed car guy who
cues.zh: 就拿 YouTube 频道 Kerlim 来说吧，他是一个自称爱车一族的美国人，

cues.en: lives in Amsterdam and has made several videos about how much he prefers driving in the
cues.zh: 住在阿姆斯特丹，做过好几个视频讲他有多喜欢在……开车

cues.en: And yet, Florida is a state that is infamous for how car-centric it is, and how hostile
cues.zh: 然而，佛罗里达州却因极其以汽车为中心而臭名昭著，

cues.en: it is for pedestrians and cyclists.
cues.zh: 对行人和骑行者也极为不友好。

cues.en: It should be a great place to drive, but it's not.
cues.zh: 按理说那里本该是个开车的好地方，但事实并非如此。

cues.en: Further proof is available from Waze, who used to collect data from their platform
cues.zh: Waze 也提供了进一步的证据，他们过去常常从自己的平台收集数据，

cues.en: to determine a driver satisfaction index each year.
cues.zh: 用以评定每年的驾驶员满意度指数。

cues.en: And they determined that the Netherlands was the best country in the world to be a driver.
cues.zh: 他们认定荷兰是全世界最适合开车司机的国家。

cues.en: This doesn't surprise me at all.
cues.zh: 这一点我完全不意外。

cues.en: Driving in the Netherlands is so pleasant.
cues.zh: 在荷兰开车真的很舒心。

cues.en: The infrastructure is of high quality and it's in great condition.
cues.zh: 基础设施质量极高，维护得也非常好。

cues.en: And in general, traffic is pretty light and flows pretty smoothly.
cues.zh: 而且大体上路况畅通，车流非常顺畅。

cues.en: Sure, there's traffic in rush hour, but rush hour is still about an hour.
cues.zh: 高峰期当然也会堵车，但早晚高峰真的就持续大约一小时。

cues.en: It's not a near-constant traffic jam spread throughout the day,
cues.zh: 绝不是全天几乎随时随地都在大堵车，

cues.en: like in most U.S. and Canadian cities.
cues.zh: 不像大多数美国和加拿大城市那样。

cues.en: It's more like a traffic hackelslach, lightly sprinkled over the week.
cues.zh: 它更像是偶尔点缀在这一周里的零星小堵。

cues.en: And there are clever approaches to temporary traffic conditions on the highway, such as
cues.zh: 而且高速公路应对临时路况的策略也非常巧妙，比如

cues.en: these rush hour lanes that open when necessary, and changing speed limits based on congestion
cues.zh: 这些必要时才会开启的高峰期车道，以及根据拥堵程度动态调整的限速，

cues.en: because drivers travelling slower have less space between cars and make better use of
cues.zh: 因为车速慢下来后车距会变小，从而能更充分地利用

cues.en: the road space.
cues.zh: 道路空间。

cues.en: It blows my mind that driving out of town on a long weekend doesn't involve getting
cues.zh: 小长假开车出城居然不会

cues.en: stuck in soul-crushing traffic, like it does in almost every other city I've lived in.
cues.zh: 被堵到怀疑人生，这真让我大开眼界，毕竟我住过的其他城市几乎无一例外。

cues.en: You'll see lots of caravans and bicycles attached to cars, but otherwise it's hardly
cues.zh: 你会看到很多房车，还有车尾架着自行车的，但除此之外，

cues.en: any different than a regular day.
cues.zh: 路况和平时几乎没什么两样。

cues.en: I've lived in cities that have a quarter of the population of Amsterdam, yet traffic
cues.zh: 我住过人口只有阿姆斯特丹四分之一的城市，但那里的交通

cues.en: in them is considerably worse.
cues.zh: 却要糟糕得多。

cues.en: This all comes down to the fundamental truth.
cues.zh: 这一切都归结于一个基本事实。

cues.en: There's no solution to traffic congestion except viable alternatives to driving.
cues.zh: 除了提供切实可行的开车替代方案，交通拥堵根本无解。

cues.en: And most Dutch cities have viable alternatives to driving for many trips, which reduces
cues.zh: 荷兰大多数城市的许多出行都有可行的开车替代方案，这减少了

cues.en: the number of cars on the road. In many Dutch cities, taking a bicycle is often the fastest
cues.zh: 路上的汽车数量。在许多荷兰城市，骑自行车往往是去往某地最快的

cues.en: way to get somewhere, because cyclists can usually take the shortest and most direct route,
cues.zh: 方式，因为骑车的人通常可以走最短、最直接的路线，

cues.en: while drivers need to take the long way around. You might think that this is bad for drivers,
cues.zh: 而开车的人则必须绕远路。你可能会觉得这对司机很不友好，

cues.en: but it's not, because if cycling wasn't faster, many of these people would be in cars, and the
cues.zh: 其实不然，因为如果骑车不比开车快，这群人很多就会改开车上路，

cues.en: streets would be so clogged with traffic that the direct route would be even slower than the
cues.zh: 街道就会被堵得水泄不通，直达路线甚至会比现在的

cues.en: indirect route is today. In fact, this was the case in Amsterdam in the 1970s.
cues.zh: 绕行路线还要慢。事实上，20世纪70年代的阿姆斯特丹就是这副光景。

cues.en: It may seem counterintuitive, but designing to prioritize walking, cycling and public
cues.zh: 这看似有悖常理，但优先考虑步行、骑行和公共

cues.en: transit actually works out better for drivers. And unsurprisingly, the Dutch cities that
cues.zh: 交通的设计，其实对司机来说反而更好。毫不意外，那些

cues.en: are the most car-centric also have the worst traffic.
cues.zh: 以汽车为中心的荷兰城市，拥堵情况也是最严重的。

cues.en: One of the things that makes driving here particularly pleasant is the fact that the
cues.zh: 在这里开车特别惬意的一个原因就是，

cues.en: a lot less. I made a video about traffic lights from the point of view of cyclists and pedestrians,
cues.zh: 等待时间少得多。我曾从骑行者和行人的角度做过一期关于交通信号灯的视频，

cues.en: but they work better for drivers too.
cues.zh: 但它们对司机来说同样更好用。

cues.en: Almost every traffic light in the Netherlands has multiple detection loops. One at the stop
cues.zh: 荷兰几乎每一个红绿灯都装有多组感应线圈。一组在停止

cues.en: line, like in many other countries, but also at least one farther back. This junction has
cues.zh: 线上，和许多国家一样，但更靠后的位置也至少有一组。这个路口

cues.en: three of them.
cues.zh: 就有三组。

cues.en: This allows the traffic control system to intelligently schedule the stop lights based
cues.zh: 这让交通控制系统能够根据各方向检测到的车流，

cues.en: on the traffic detected from each direction.
cues.zh: 智能调度红绿灯。

cues.en: For example, you will very often see the traffic light turn red, just as the last car passes the stop line.
cues.zh: 比如，你经常会看到最后一辆车刚过停止线，红灯就亮了。

cues.en: This is because the control system uses the farther detection loop to determine that there isn't another car approaching,
cues.zh: 这是因为控制系统利用较远处的感应线圈判断出没有其他车开过来，

cues.en: so it's safe to change the light to red early and let another direction turn red.
cues.zh: 所以提前变红灯是安全的，同时可以让另一个方向变红……

cues.en: go while there's a gap in traffic.
cues.zh: 趁车流出现空当赶紧通行。

cues.en: It also works to turn a light green early if it detects your car or bike is approaching
cues.zh: 如果它检测到你的汽车或自行车正在接近，也能提前变绿灯，

cues.en: when it's safe to stop traffic in other directions.
cues.zh: 只要此时安全截停其他方向的车流即可。

cues.en: Another difference is that, in the US and Canada, traffic lights are stupid and go all
cues.zh: 另一个区别是，在美国和加拿大，红绿灯很死板，

cues.en: green in one direction followed by all green in the other direction.
cues.zh: 全是一个方向全绿，接着另一个方向全绿。

cues.en: But here in the Netherlands, traffic lights work in multiple phases, so there are many
cues.zh: 但在荷兰这里，红绿灯是多相位的，所以有很多

cues.en: different combinations possible for things like dedicated right turns and left turns
cues.zh: 不同的组合形式，比如同时允许专属的右转和左转。

cues.en: simultaneously. This not only speeds up waiting times at traffic lights, it also
cues.zh: 这不仅缩短了等红灯的时间，

cues.en: makes turning much less dangerous and stressful because when you have a green
cues.zh: 还大大降低了转弯的危险和压力，因为只要亮起绿箭头，

cues.en: arrow you're almost always clear to turn. In particular, the left turn across
cues.zh: 你几乎总能安全顺畅地转弯。特别是横穿

cues.en: traffic on a strode is one of the most dangerous and stressful driving maneuvers
cues.zh: 对向车流在商业干道（stroad）上左转，是美加两国

cues.en: in the United States and Canada. I almost never need to perform a turn like this
cues.zh: 最危险、最让人紧张的驾驶操作之一。

cues.en: in the Netherlands. Speaking of strodes, there are almost none in the Netherlands
cues.zh: 在荷兰我几乎从来不用做这种转弯。说到商业干道，荷兰几乎根本就没有

cues.en: as I've talked about in previous videos.
cues.zh: 正如我在之前的视频中聊过的那样。

cues.en: This means that when you're on a road,
cues.zh: 这意味着当你在路上行驶时，

cues.en: there are very few side streets,
cues.zh: 很少会有支路、

cues.en: driveways, or crossings to slow you down.
cues.zh: 车道出入口或路口让你慢下来。

cues.en: This has so many benefits that it's hard to list them all.
cues.zh: 这样做的好处多到数不胜数。

cues.en: In general, the lack of strobes
cues.zh: 总的来说，没有斯创路（Stroad）

cues.en: keeps traffic moving smoothly,
cues.zh: 能让交通保持顺畅，

cues.en: and even if the speed limit is lower,
cues.zh: 即使限速更低，

cues.en: your average speed is much higher
cues.zh: 你的平均车速反而要快得多，

cues.en: because there are fewer cars
cues.zh: 因为进出主路的车辆更少，

cues.en: merging in and out and fewer traffic lights.
cues.zh: 红绿灯也更少。

cues.en: This is something that people don't appreciate enough.
cues.zh: 这一点很多人都没意识到。

cues.en: Strobes have so many driveways
cues.zh: 斯创路有太多的出入口

cues.en: and side streets that require merging into high-speed traffic that some driveways inevitably
cues.zh: 和支路，都需要汇入高速车流，这不可避免地会导致一些车道出入口

cues.en: get traffic build-ups from people trying to exit.
cues.zh: 因为大家试图开出来而拥堵不堪。

cues.en: The solution is to install a traffic light, which is why there are so many traffic lights
cues.zh: 解决办法就是装个红绿灯，这也是为什么北美大多数城市

cues.en: in most North American cities.
cues.zh: 会有这么多红绿灯的原因。

cues.en: In the newest Strong Towns book, Confessions of a Recovering Engineer, author Chuck Morone
cues.zh: 在 Strong Towns 的新书《Confessions of a Recovering Engineer》中，作者 Chuck Morone

cues.en: measured his average speed at rush hour and found that it was about 16 kilometers per
cues.zh: 测算了自己在高峰期的平均车速，发现大约只有每小时

cues.en: hour.
cues.zh: 16公里。

cues.en: Actually, it was an average of less than 10 miles per hour, but I'm converting everything
cues.zh: 实际上平均时速还不到10英里，不过我都换算成公制单位了，

cues.en: the metric here because imperial units are stupid. So, despite the roads having a speed limit of 50
cues.zh: 因为英制单位实在太反人类了。所以，尽管道路限速在50

cues.en: kilometers per hour or more, his average speed was less than 16 because of all the traffic lights.
cues.zh: 公里每小时甚至更高，但因为全是红绿灯，他的平均车速还不到16。

cues.en: And this was in a tiny town of only 14,000 people. Incidentally, 16 kilometers an hour is the average
cues.zh: 而这还是在一个仅有1.4万人口的小镇上。顺便提一句，时速16公里恰好也是阿姆斯特丹

cues.en: speed of a cyclist in Amsterdam, because bicycle routes are designed to avoid traffic lights and
cues.zh: 自行车的平均时速，因为当地的骑行路线设计避开了红绿灯，

cues.en: to keep cyclists moving.
cues.zh: 能让骑行者一直往前开。

cues.en: This really shows you how backwards American traffic engineering is when the average speed
cues.zh: 这充分说明了美国的交通工程有多落后：

cues.en: of a car in a small town in the US is the same as a bicycle in the largest and busiest
cues.zh: 一个美国小镇上的汽车平均速度，竟然跟荷兰最大、

cues.en: city in the Netherlands.
cues.zh: 最繁忙都市里的自行车差不多。

cues.en: I had the same experience when driving in my hometown this summer.
cues.zh: 今年夏天在老家开车时，我也有同样的经历。

cues.en: I was constantly sitting at red lights when I was driving simply because there are so
cues.zh: 开车时我总是在等红灯，纯粹是因为红绿灯

cues.en: many of them.
cues.zh: 实在太多了。

cues.en: And if there aren't traffic lights, there are stop signs.
cues.zh: 就算没有红绿灯，也有停步标志（Stop signs）。

cues.en: So many stop signs.
cues.zh: 多到数不清的停步标志。

cues.en: Instead of designing proper traffic calming, North American traffic engineers just put stop signs everywhere to slow down drivers.
cues.zh: 北美的交通工程师并没有去设计合理的交通宁静化措施，而是到处立停步标志来让司机减速。

cues.en: I already made a previous video about why I hate stop signs and why they shouldn't be required at all, especially for cyclists.
cues.zh: 我之前就做过一期视频，讲了我为什么讨厌停步标志，以及为什么根本不该强制要求停车，尤其是对骑行者而言。

cues.en: But yeah, it's so nice to drive through the Netherlands and not see any stop signs at all.
cues.zh: 不过话说回来，在荷兰开车真的很爽，一路上一个停步标志都看不到。

cues.en: And the very, very, very few times you see one, it's actually necessary.
cues.zh: 就算极罕见地碰到一个，那也确实是有必要的。

cues.en: Of course, there are many intersections with roundabouts too, which is even better.
cues.zh: 当然，那里还有很多带环岛的十字路口，这就更棒了。

cues.en: Then there's almost no waiting at all, and traffic flows even more efficiently.
cues.zh: 那时几乎完全不用等待，车流也会更加顺畅。

cues.en: Though roundabouts can get backed up if there's too much car traffic, so they don't work everywhere.
cues.zh: 不过如果车流量太大，环岛也会堵塞，所以它们并非哪里都适用。

cues.en: Of course, the Dutch have a solution for that too, which is turbo roundabouts,
cues.zh: 当然，荷兰人对此也有应对方案，那就是“涡轮环岛”（turbo roundabouts），

cues.en: but they deserve their own video some day.
cues.zh: 但这改天值得单独做一期视频来聊。

cues.en: I would gladly take a road with a lower maximum speed limit,
cues.zh: 我宁愿选择一条最高限速更低的道路，

cues.en: But if that road design means that I achieve a higher average speed, and that is exactly
cues.zh: 只要这种道路设计能让我获得更高的平均速度即可，而这恰恰就是

cues.en: what I experience driving in the Netherlands.
cues.zh: 我在荷兰开车时的亲身体验。

cues.en: I made a video about speed limits recently, but what's relevant here is that speed limits
cues.zh: 我最近做了一期关于限速的视频，但这里要说的是，荷兰的限速

cues.en: in the Netherlands mostly make sense.
cues.zh: 大部分都非常合理。

cues.en: Different streets with different speed limits are designed differently, so you rarely need
cues.zh: 限速不同的街道设计也各不相同，所以你很少需要

cues.en: to check your speed.
cues.zh: 低头去看自己的车速。

cues.en: The speed that feels right on a given street is usually the correct one.
cues.zh: 在一条特定街道上让你感觉舒服的车速，通常就是合适的速度。

cues.en: When I was driving in my hometown this summer, I was constantly needing to check what the
cues.zh: 今年夏天我在老家开车时，总得时不时去确认

cues.en: speed limit was, because everything is designed like a giant strode, yet the speed limit could
cues.zh: 限速是多少，因为所有道路都被设计得像巨大的“路街结合体”，而限速却可能

cues.en: be anywhere from 40 km an hour to 80 km an hour with no difference in road design.
cues.zh: 在40到80公里每小时之间随意变化，道路设计却没有任何区别。

cues.en: Another factor that makes driving in the Netherlands less stressful is that the
cues.zh: 让在荷兰开车压力较小的另一个因素是，

cues.en: drivers themselves are better. There are many aspects of this, such as stricter licensing
cues.zh: 司机本身的素质更好。这涵盖很多方面，比如更严格的驾照

cues.en: requirements, but I believe the single most important factor is that, in most Dutch cities,
cues.zh: 考核要求，但我认为最关键的一点在于，在大多数荷兰城市里，

cues.en: there are viable alternatives to driving.
cues.zh: 除了开车，还有其他切实可行的出行选择。

cues.en: This means that the only people who are driving are those people who want to drive, or those people who need to drive.
cues.zh: 这意味着，真正在路上开车的，只有那些想开车或必须开车的人。

cues.en: Most people who live in a Dutch city can make many trips by walking, cycling, or public transit.
cues.zh: 大多数住在荷兰城市的人，很多日常出行都可以靠步行、骑车或公共交通解决。

cues.en: Even if somebody drives to work, they may still get their grocery shopping by bicycle,
cues.zh: 哪怕有人开车上班，他们可能仍然会骑自行车去买菜，

cues.en: walk to a doctor's office,
cues.zh: 步行去看医生，

cues.en: appointment or take public transportation to a football game.
cues.zh: 或是坐公共交通去看足球赛。

cues.en: In particular, shopping by bicycle or by walking is a very low stress activity, and it's usually
cues.zh: 尤其是骑车或步行去购物，压力非常小，而且通常

cues.en: done when you're on the way home from somewhere else, so it doesn't even feel like a chore.
cues.zh: 都是在从别处回家的路上顺便完成的，甚至让人觉得根本不算件杂事。

cues.en: In car-dependent places, you need to drive for everything, so even the most trivial
cues.zh: 而在依赖汽车的地方，干什么都得开车，所以哪怕是最微不足道
